title: Prefill credit decomposition and windowed gating for burst-smooth continuous batching
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
We propose a new admission control primitive — prefill credit decomposition — combined with a windowed gating policy to smooth short bursts and improve kernel coalescence. The goal is to reduce tail latency from microbursts while preserving throughput and enabling better kernel selection decisions (fewer mismatched kernel launches and fewer tiny token batches).

Motivation:
Current continuous batching suffers from oscillations when many short prefill-heavy requests arrive simultaneously. That causes: (1) many small kernel launches with poor amortization, (2) decode starvation when prefill credits are exhausted unevenly, and (3) attention cache churn when attention prewarm decisions are made per-request. Existing admission approaches try to shape batch size heuristically; we need a per-request credit model that separates prefill vs decode budget and enforces a small-time-window gate to absorb bursts.

Design (high level):
- Credit decomposition: when a request arrives, compute two reservation tokens: prefill_credit and decode_credit based on request metadata (estimated prefill tokens, decode ceiling, priority). These are virtual credits tracked per-tenant on the node.
- Windowed gating: credits are consumed against a sliding window reservoir (configurable window_ms). The reservoir has two lanes (prefill and decode) with independent refill rates tuned from telemetry. The window acts as a short-term rate limiter smoothing microbursts without rejecting requests.
- Kernel coalescence hints: when prefill_credit is granted, we tag the request with a kernel_hint (e.g., small-prefill, large-prefill, attention-wide) derived from batch-size and attention-length estimators. The admission layer aggregates compatible hints to trigger kernel coalescing and warmup.
- Backpressure and fallback: if reservoir is exhausted, we offer three graceful degradations in order: (1) defer request to next window tick (introduce a controlled latency holdback up to max_hold_ms), (2) fall back to a low-memory quantized kernel variant, (3) reject with 429 when SLO budgets are exceeded.

Telemetry & metrics:
We will emit new metrics: prefill_credit_granted, prefill_credit_denied, window_hold_ms_histogram, kernel_hint_coalesce_ratio, microburst_loss_rate, per-tenant_reservoir_utilization. These feed a new dashboard and an alert when kernel_hint_coalesce_ratio drops >20% vs baseline.

Implementation plan:
1) Admission layer framework: add credit bookkeeping to the local admission store + per-node reservoir (proto + state machine).
2) Estimator service: lightweight estimator in the serving path to predict prefill token count and attention window length (starts with heuristic, then ML tuning).
3) Kernel hint tagging & aggregation logic in batcher to group compatible requests before kernel selection.
4) Fallback orchestration to select alternate kernel or defer queue.
5) End-to-end tests and perf comparisons vs baseline.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.prefill_credit_decomposition.
- Start with internal canary on a small Dedicated pool (synthesize microburst traffic).
- Collect metrics for 2 weeks, tune reservoir refill and window_ms, then expand to 25% of prod traffic.
- Full rollout conditional on tail-95/99 improvements and no throughput regression >2%.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overly conservative reservoir settings increase added latency (holdback) and may hurt p50. We will tune for p99 improvement while keeping p50 regressions <3%.
- Incorrect estimator predictions may misallocate credits. Mitigation: degrade to safe heuristics and add online learning.
- Complexity in kernel hint matching could increase scheduling latency; keep matching O(1) with hash-buckets by (model, quant, attention-band).

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for credit accounting and reservoir lifecycle.
- Integration harness that replays production arrival traces with injected microbursts (use trace: replay-2026-01-microbursts).
- Perf jobs comparing baseline vs feature: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel launch rate, token-per-kernel, and cost-per-token.

Artifacts & references:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/CB-120/prefill-credit-decomp (draft)
- Perf replay trace: gs://redwood-traces/replay-2026-01-microbursts.tar.gz
- Initial estimator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4891
- Batcher kernel-hint PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4917

Success criteria:
- kernel_hint_coalesce_ratio increases by >=25% in canary pools
- p99 latency improves by >=15% on microburst-heavy workloads without throughput drop >2%
- No increase in error rate or stability incidents during 30-day canary
